When Does Regression Adjustment Estimate the
Global Treatment Effect under Network Interference?
Anonymous Author(s)
Affiliation

Abstract
Network interference breaks the usual analysis of randomised experiments. A
standard estimator of the global average treatment effect (GATE) regresses the
outcome on own treatment and a function of neighbours’ treatments, then predicts
at all-treated and all-control. We ask how accurate it is and when it should not be
used, treating it as extrapolation from the exposures the experiment produced to
the two global corners. In simulations with exactly known GATE (six interference
mechanisms, synthetic and two real graphs, Bernoulli and cluster designs), the
variance follows OLS leverage (RMSE slopes −0.50 in n, +0.55 in 1+d for mean
degree d). The bias is set by the response at the corners, which the data inside
the observed exposure range do not identify (our reading, not a separate test): a
formula that knows the mechanism matches the realised bias in 82% of cells, and its
dependence on degree differs by mechanism. Regression beats difference-in-means
in 78% of grid cells at moderate noise (31% at high noise); the spillover share
above which it wins rises with degree (about 0.1, 0.19, 0.38 at d = 5, 20, 80), with
a threshold mechanism as an exception on synthetic graphs that does not carry over
to real ones. Two expectations fail: none of the data-computable scores we tried
predicts the bias better than a constant, and nominal 95% intervals cover 74% of
Bernoulli cells. On a sample of cells, flexible learners do not beat the regression,
except under the threshold mechanism. All outcomes are simulated.

shown.message:
I checked the `main` build against the venue requirements, and the main text is within 9 pages. One problem remains: repository and role names appear in files that belong with the code archive. I opened `paper-repo`#11 about it.

- **Page limit:** 24 pages, with the References heading at the top of page 10. The main text is 9 pages and holds 5 figures. The checklist has 16 items with no placeholders. The text has no unresolved references. The only Type 3 font is the template's own.
- **Anonymity:** the paper sources, the checklist and `code/` are clean. These files are not:
  - `REPRODUCE.md`, line 108
  - `figures/gen/style.py`, lines 3–4
  - `figures/gen/common.py`, line 24
  - `README.md`
  - `figures/CAPTIONS.md`

  If the anonymous ZIP is built from any of these, it breaks the double-blind rule. I found no packaging step in `paper-repo`. `experiment-repo` has one, but I didn't read what it scrubs.
- **Abstract length:** about 235 words, inside the accepted-paper sample's 169–266 range. My recommendation was at most about 220, which isn't a venue rule, so I only noted it in the issue.

The issue asks `figtab-repo` to fix its generator files and `internal-review-repo` to check the archive for those names before a version is approved.
